First, note the given date: 05-06-1795 (likely DD-MM-YYYY format → 1795-06-05 in ISO).  

Subtract 49 weeks and 6 days:  
49 weeks = 49 × 7 = 343 days.  
Plus 6 days = 349 days total to subtract.  

1795 is not a leap year (divisible by 4 but not by 400, and not century leap).  
June 5, 1795 minus 349 days:  

Go back into 1794:  
From June 5 to Jan 1, 1795:  
April (30), May (31), March (31), February (28), January (31) → but easier:  
Days from Jan 1 to June 5, 1795:  
Jan 31 + Feb 28 + Mar 31 + Apr 30 + May 31 + 5 days in June = 31+28+31+30+31+5 = 156 days.  

So June 5 is 156th day of 1795 (non-leap).  
349 − 156 = 193 days into previous year (1794).  

1794 is not leap (not divisible by 4).  
Days in 1794 after Jan 1:  
Jan 31, Feb 28, Mar 31, Apr 30, May 31, Jun 30, Jul 31 = 31+28+31+30+31+30+31 = 212 days by end of July.  
We need 193 days into 1794:  
Jan 31 (31), Feb 28 (59), Mar 31 (90), Apr 30 (120), May 31 (151), Jun 30 (181), July has 31 days: 181 + 12 = 193 → July 12, 1794.  

Check: 193rd day of 1794 = Jan 31 (31) + Feb 28 (59) + Mar 31 (90) + Apr 30 (120) + May 31 (151) + Jun 30 (181) → July 12 = 181 + 12 = 193.  

FINAL_ANSWER: 1794-07-12
